title: Ang 485–487: Namdev, Ravidas, Dhanna
hookLine: everything is Gobind, sandalwood and castor
tomorrow: who gets the very last word in the raga of Asa?

cards: Stand next to someone wearing strong perfume in an elevator, and it's on your jacket by lunch. You didn't spray a thing. You just stood close.

On ang 486, a man who hauled dead cattle for a living stands close to something, and comes away carrying its scent. And on the very next page, a farmer hears his story and stops what he's doing. What did he hear?

teach.b: Three Bhagats come near the end of Asa. First Namdev, with one thread. In paraphrase: everything is Gobind, everything is Gobind; without Gobind there is no one.
The One runs through the many like a single thread through a string of beads, like water through every wave and bubble. Then Ravidas, and his picture is the elevator.
In paraphrase: you are sandalwood, and I'm the poor castor plant growing beside you. From a low tree I've grown tall, because your fragrance now lives in me. Castor is a plain, scrubby plant.
Sandalwood is the wood people burn for its perfume. Ravidas never says he turned into sandalwood. He says he stood close, and the scent stayed.
Then, on ang 487, Dhanna, and here's the scene. He names them one by one. Namdev, whose mind was soaked in Gobind.
Kabir, who left his weaving for love. Ravidas, who carried away dead cattle. Sain, the barber.
Each one, the hymn says, met the Lord.
And Dhanna, a farmer, hears it all and turns to devotion himself. So that's what he heard: a weaver, a leatherworker, a barber, all carrying the scent.
Nobody in that list got in by birth.
They got in by standing close. And the Granth keeps their words right beside the Gurus' own.

how: Sikhs reading the Granth in order reach the Bhagats' hymns at the end of each raga, after the Gurus'; in Asa, Kabir, Namdev, Ravidas and Dhanna come before Farid, and their hymns are sung in kirtan like the rest.

o: the last page of the Bhagat Kabir's hymns
the page where Guru Nanak opens the raga of Asa
the page where Namdev sings that everything is Gobind

games.q: who sings what — tap the pairs.
p: a farmer who heard the names

s: the Granth holds only the Gurus' own hymns
it holds Bhagats too: Namdev, Ravidas and Dhanna sing near the end of Asa.
Ravidas says he turned into sandalwood
he stays the castor plant; the sandalwood's fragrance comes to live in him.
Dhanna's hymn names a barber and a man who carried dead cattle
Sain the barber and Ravidas; each, the hymn says, met the Lord.

games.q: a new kid hangs back by the door of your gurdwara's langar kitchen, unsure if he can help. he isn't Sikh. what fits ang 486–487?
o: hand him a ladle and let him stand beside you.
point him to the line to eat; serving is for members.
let him watch for a few weeks until he knows the rules.
games.why: Ravidas stood near the sandalwood and the scent stayed; Dhanna's list runs from a weaver to a barber. standing close is the way in.

practice: Find something with a scent near you: a spice jar, hand soap, a tea bag, the collar of a jacket. Breathe it in slowly once, then rest that hand near your face for the sit.
Notice the scent is still with you after the jar is gone; if you'd like, read Ravidas's lines on ang 486 first.

wordCard.voice: Ang 485. The page where Namdev sings that everything is Gobind, opening the run that leads to Ravidas's sandalwood and Dhanna's list of names.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chandan, sandalwood; Ravidas's picture on ang 486.

carryVoice: Keep it close: sandalwood, and stand near it long enough that it's on you too. See you tomorrow.
